scope: Object-disjoint HRDexDB Wan-Animate-2 raw validation baseline
summary: Using an apple train-object Inspire F1 reference, raw Wan-Animate-2 fails both validation objects; only target identity remains high, so held-out test objects stay sealed.
evidence: Banana validation scores are motion 0.397773, identity 0.969381, object 0.003866, and temporal 0.116649.
Beige-brush core scores are motion 0.373124, identity 0.979186, and temporal 0.024394; the low-chroma object tracker is unresolved, so the object gate remains failed rather than fabricated.
Both runs use seed 42, the same train-object reference image, 81 frames, 10 distilled steps, guidance 1.0, and physical A800 GPUs 2-3.
Paired validation robot videos are used only as evaluator references and never generation inputs.
lessons: The strong Hand2Dex identity result does not generalize to object-disjoint motion, object interaction, or temporal consistency.
A low-chroma object must use geometry/segmentation evidence; color-tracker failure is an unresolved hard gate.
limitations: Only two validation objects and one seed were evaluated.
The current raw method is rejected before test-set confirmation.
next_actions: Develop object-pose/mesh-projected masks and robot-geometry conditioning on train/validation objects; do not open box_pink or cactus for the unchanged raw method.
